title: What to expect as UN General Assembly convenes amid Iran war
gist: Preview of the 2026 UN General Assembly held amid the US-Iran war: the US granted visas to Iran's core delegation but denied the Palestinian delegation, and the summit is expected to serve as a backchannel venue where Gulf mediators may pass messages on reopening the Iran-blockaded Strait of Hormuz, while Houthi seizures near Bab el-Mandeb give Iran's camp leverage over a second chokepoint.

insights.claim: The UN General Assembly is expected to serve as a backchannel for US-Iran messaging, with senior Iranian officials meeting counterparts from Oman, Qatar and other Gulf states while Trump meets GCC leaders.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth Hagedorn
insights.so_what: Watch late-September UNGA sideline meetings for headlines that could move oil risk premia on any Hormuz de-escalation.
insights.quote: There will be plenty of opportunity for messages to be passed

insights.claim: Stimson Center fellow Barbara Slavin sees possible progress on managing the Strait of Hormuz coming out of UNGA-week diplomacy.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth Hagedorn
insights.so_what: Any Hormuz management framework would be the single biggest downside catalyst for crude and tanker rates.
insights.locator: There will be plenty of opportunity

insights.claim: Iranian President Pezeshkian is personally a proponent of a diplomatic resolution but is expected to deliver firm anti-US rhetoric at the UN because he represents the whole system, so the speech itself is a weak signal of negotiating posture.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth Hagedorn
insights.so_what: Discount hawkish UN rhetoric from Tehran; track private channels (Oman, Qatar) instead.
insights.quote: But he is going to be there representing the system as a whole, and so he has to be quite firm.
insights.locator: Pezeshkian is likely to employ familiar

insights.claim: The US granted last-minute visas to Iran's core delegation, including Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Araghchi, but under travel restrictions and a ban on buying luxury goods; the delegation is smaller than last year's.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth Hagedorn
insights.so_what: Keeping the Iranian channel physically open in New York signals Washington has not fully closed the diplomatic door.
insights.locator: All eyes will be on the Iranians

insights.claim: Iran has effectively blockaded the Strait of Hormuz since the war began and conditions reopening on removal of US sanctions and war-damage compensation, demands the Trump administration rejects.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth Hagedorn
insights.so_what: The gap between Iranian conditions and US positions implies the Hormuz disruption is not near resolution; keep oil supply-risk hedges.
insights.locator: Iran has effectively blockaded the strait

insights.claim: Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and shipping, plus their seizure of islands near Bab el-Mandeb, give Iran and its allies leverage over two global chokepoints simultaneously.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth Hagedorn
insights.so_what: With both Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb at risk, Red Sea bypass routes for Gulf exports lose value; shipping insurance and freight premia stay elevated.
insights.quote: giving Iran and its allies leverage over two global chokepoints
insights.locator: In addition to attacks on Saudi energy

insights.claim: The US State Department denied visas to the Palestinian delegation, accusing the PLO and Palestinian Authority of glorifying terrorism, so Mahmoud Abbas will address the Assembly virtually for a second straight year.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth Hagedorn
insights.so_what: Highlights the widening US-Europe split on Palestine policy.

insights.claim: France, the UK and Canada are hosting a high-level two-state-solution meeting and earlier this month jointly announced sanctions banning imports of goods from Israeli settlements in the West Bank.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth Hagedorn
insights.so_what: Settlement-goods import bans are an emerging trade-sanction vector; watch for companies with West Bank supply chains facing European market access risk.
insights.locator: Earlier this month, the three countries

insights.claim: Richard Gowan of the International Crisis Group argues the Palestinian question will loom less large at this UNGA because the Security Council effectively handed Gaza responsibility to the Trump-led Board of Peace.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth Hagedorn
insights.so_what: Diplomatic attention on Gaza is shifting away from the UN to a US-led body, concentrating outcome risk on Washington.
insights.locator: Richard Gowan, the International Crisis Group

insights.claim: The Board of Peace has struggled since January to implement the next Gaza ceasefire phase: Hamas disarmament, Israeli troop withdrawal and deployment of an international stabilization force.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth Hagedorn
insights.so_what: Stalled Gaza phase two keeps reconstruction-related opportunities and regional normalization on hold.

insights.claim: With Israeli elections on Oct. 27, Netanyahu is expected to deliver an especially charged UN speech aimed primarily at a domestic audience, likely targeting alleged UN bias.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth Hagedorn
insights.so_what: Treat Netanyahu's UN rhetoric as campaign messaging ahead of the Oct. 27 vote rather than a policy shift.
insights.quote: performing primarily for a domestic audience
insights.locator: With the Israeli elections on Oct. 27

insights.claim: The Trump administration has cut tranches of UN funding, yet Trump will address the General Assembly, while Xi Jinping skips the UN to meet Trump in Washington on Thursday.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth Hagedorn
insights.so_what: A bilateral Trump-Xi meeting outranks the multilateral forum; watch it for trade and tech outcomes.

insights.claim: Settler violence in the West Bank has risen sharply in 2026 and Netanyahu's right-wing government has overseen settlement expansion.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth Hagedorn
insights.so_what: Rising West Bank instability feeds European sanction momentum against Israel.
insights.locator: Settler violence there has risen sharply
